subject: GPU fleet thermostat: sizing multipliers & cutover plan for dedicated swap

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted → Dedicated swap: request for short-run workload samples

Hi Helen —

Thanks again for the chat earlier. To validate the sizing proposal and lock a cutover window we need: a 7-day sample of peak-hour traces (request/second, median sequence length, 95th percentile seq len), a list of heavy endpoints (rerank, multi-turn chat, embeddings), and any scheduled nightly batch jobs. If possible, please include a small CSV with token counts per API key / route — that'll let us calculate realistic KV-cache reuse and batching potential.

We're planning a light rightsize pass on our side (multipliers applied by route + quantization guidance) and a short staging run (3h soak). If you can share data by EOD Monday I can get a draft cutover timeline back to you by Thursday.

Attachments: none (please attach the CSV reply)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-14T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted → Dedicated swap: request for short-run workload samples

Forwarding Helen's export. Quick internal ask: can we run the multiplier model from the rightsize library (config v2.1) and produce two options — conservative (SLA-focused) and aggressive (cost-first) — with explicit GPU counts, target p99 latency, and expected token/unit cost?

Preliminary observations on my quick pass: with 95th seq len near 930 we should expect higher KV cache pressure; propose we model a "thermostat" approach: baseline pool + surge buffer that scales on 5-min windows (multiplier +1.6 for peak planning, +1.1 for overnight batch). Also add a canary lane with 10% traffic at day 2 to validate QoE.

Deliverables requested:
- spreadsheet with per-route multipliers and GPU slot estimates (proposed-rightsize-multipliers.xlsx)
- staged cutover playbook (cutover-playbook-20250818.pdf) including rollback criteria and canary smoke tests
- recommended quantization profile (FP16 vs 4bit) per model variant

Ben/Karthik — can you own the spreadsheet and run the 3h staging soak on a pre-prod cluster? Grace — please draft the playbook sections for rollback criteria & monitoring checks (traces, token-level cost deltas, 95th tail latency).

Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Helen Zhao <helen.zhao@oracledg.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-16T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GPU fleet thermostat: sizing multipliers & cutover plan for dedicated swap

Hi all —

Attached is the proposed spreadsheet and the cutover playbook draft. High-level summary:
- Conservative plan (SLA-prioritized): 18 GPU slots (A100-equivalents), surge buffer +60% (multiplier 1.6) for the 90-minute peak window. Expected p95 inference latency: 220ms; p99 under 400ms.
- Aggressive plan (cost-prioritized): 12 GPU slots, surge buffer +30% (multiplier 1.3), rely on more aggressive batching & 4-bit quantization for embedding-heavy routes. Expected p95 latency: 300ms; p99 ~520ms.

Staging run notes: we ran a 3h soak yesterday in pre-prod with the conservative profile and saw stable KV hits and no memory OOMs. Canary recommendation: 10% traffic swap for 24h, validate error rate <0.1% and token-cost delta <6% before 100% cutover.

Attachments: proposed-rightsize-multipliers.xlsx, cutover-playbook-20250818.pdf

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Zhao <helen.zhao@oracledg.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-18T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final: proposed cutover window & acceptance criteria (Fri 2025-08-22)

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the staging work. Based on Ben's findings we'd like to propose the following plan:

Cutover window: Friday 2025-08-22 02:00–06:00 UTC (US overnight)
Plan: dry-run on pre-prod Thursday 21st 22:00 UTC (3h soak) → canary swap 10% traffic Friday 02:00 UTC → monitor for 24h → 100% swap earliest Saturday 02:00 UTC if canary green.
Acceptance & rollback criteria (short):
- Canary error rate <= 0.1% sustained for 1h
- p99 latency delta <= +40% vs hosted baseline
- Token-level cost delta within expected band from spreadsheet (conservative plan: +/-8%)
- If any gating fails, automatic rollback to hosted route and capacity healing within 15 minutes

Attachments: cutover-playbook-20250818.pdf, proposed-rightsize-multipliers.xlsx

Please reply with ACK or suggest alternative windows by EOD Wednesday. If ACK, we'll raise the Dedicated activation ticket and provision the reserved pool on Monday morning.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: cutover-playbook-20250818.pdf, proposed-rightsize-multipliers.xlsx)

From: Helen Zhao <helen.zhao@oracledg.com>

Subject: Re: Final: proposed cutover window & acceptance criteria (Fri 2025-08-22)

ACK. Friday window works for us. We'll schedule infra on our side and confirm the dry-run Thursday afternoon. One question: for the conservative plan, are you expecting us to keep a small cold-cache buffer for 48 hours post-cutover or do you recommend warming aggressively? We'd prefer to warm gradually if that lowers risk.

—Helen
